chains.title: C250T creates a de novo ETS site bound by GABPA (with GABPB1), activating the TERT promoter
chains.element: TERT core promoter cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), chr5:1294945-1295294

links.claim: The G>A change is predicted to create an ETS core (GGAA) and the alt allele is proposed to bind more strongly. Within the ETS binding-specificity group I pick GABPA because ENCODE ChIP-seq shows GABPA peaks that physically contain chr5:1295135 in two biosamples (HepG2, SK-N-SH) and because GABPA is well expressed in glioblastoma lines (rank 303/1626 TFs). Caveat: those ChIP peaks are from cells presumed wild-type at this position, so they show the promoter is a GABPA-occupied region but not an allele-specific gain; no QBiC-SELEX row or detail lookup was available, so coverage is not_checked and the allele direction remains an inference, not a measurement.

The variant lies in an active promoter-like element (Ensembl ENSR5_832QG; ENCODE cCRE EH38E3622530, PLS) with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac maxima across biosamples; z-scores are maxima, not glioblastoma-specific.

The element is the TERT core promoter (TERT TSS 0.0 kb; TERT listed as nearby gene for the cCRE), so TERT is the most likely cis target rather than CLPTM1L (50 kb). This is proximity plus promoter annotation only, with no eQTL or CRISPRi link.

TERT promoter mutations are among the most frequent alterations in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and GABPA is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context (15.52 TPM, 58th percentile across lines), so the proposed activator is present where the mutation occurs. The literature quote does not name C250T specifically.

Increased TERT transcription would restore telomerase activity and avert senescence; TERT promoter mutations are the commonest noncoding alteration in melanoma and loss of TERT triggers senescence. Note DepMap short-term CRISPR shows essentially no TERT dependency (median -0.00 in CNS lines), consistent with telomere-driven phenotypes being slow and not captured in such screens.

PMID 42804732 (2026): SNP rs2853669 potentially elevates the risk of glioblastoma development and leads to worse prognosis when in cis with mutant TERT promoter in a Japanese cohort.
PMID 42807929 (2026): USP10 stabilizes FOXM1 through KAT5-mediated acetylation to suppress cell senescence and promote melanoma malignant progression.
PMID 42859331 (2026): CDKN2A deletion associated with poor prognosis in patients with TERT promoter wild-type, IDH wild-type glioblastoma.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
